words.definition: a carbon-containing compound associated with living organisms, usually containing carbon-hydrogen bonds
words.example: Glucose and lipids are examples of organic compounds found in cells.

words.definition: the chain or ring of carbon atoms that forms the structural framework of an organic molecule
words.example: Different carbon skeletons allow organic molecules to have many shapes and functions.

words.definition: a chemical bond formed when atoms share pairs of electrons
words.example: Carbon atoms form covalent bonds with hydrogen, oxygen and other carbon atoms.

words.definition: a small molecular subunit that can join with others to form a larger molecule
words.example: Glucose monomers can be joined to form polysaccharides.

words.definition: a large molecule made from many repeating or related monomer units
words.example: Cellulose is a polymer of glucose.

words.definition: a reaction that joins molecules while releasing a small molecule, usually water
words.example: A condensation reaction can join two monosaccharides.

words.definition: a reaction that uses water to split a covalent bond in a larger molecule
words.example: Hydrolysis breaks polysaccharides into smaller sugars.

words.definition: a single sugar unit that cannot be hydrolysed into a simpler carbohydrate
words.example: Glucose is a monosaccharide used in respiration.

words.definition: a six-carbon monosaccharide that is an important energy source and building block
words.japanese: グルコース・ブドウ糖
words.example: Plants produce glucose during photosynthesis.

words.definition: a carbohydrate polymer composed of many monosaccharide units
words.example: Starch, glycogen and cellulose are polysaccharides.

words.definition: a glucose-storage polysaccharide found mainly in plants
words.example: Plants store excess glucose as starch.

words.definition: a highly branched glucose-storage polysaccharide found mainly in animals and fungi
words.example: Liver and muscle cells store glucose as glycogen.

words.definition: a structural polysaccharide of beta-glucose that forms plant cell walls
words.example: Cellulose fibres strengthen plant cell walls.

words.definition: a protein with one or more carbohydrate chains attached
words.example: Cell-surface glycoproteins can act in recognition and signalling.

words.definition: a diverse group of mostly hydrophobic biological molecules that includes fats, phospholipids and steroids
words.example: Lipids can store energy and form cell membranes.

words.definition: a lipid consisting of glycerol joined to three fatty acids
words.japanese: トリグリセリド・中性脂肪
words.example: Triglycerides are stored in adipose tissue as an energy reserve.

words.definition: a three-carbon alcohol that forms the backbone of triglycerides and many phospholipids
words.example: One glycerol molecule combines with three fatty acids to form a triglyceride.

words.definition: an organic acid with a hydrocarbon chain and a terminal carboxyl group
words.example: Fatty acids differ in chain length and degree of saturation.

words.definition: an amphipathic lipid with a phosphate-containing hydrophilic head and hydrophobic fatty-acid tails
words.example: Phospholipids spontaneously form bilayers in water.

words.definition: a fatty acid whose hydrocarbon chain contains no carbon-carbon double bonds
words.example: Saturated fatty acids are usually straight and can pack closely together.

words.definition: a fatty acid containing one carbon-carbon double bond
words.example: Oleic acid is a common monounsaturated fatty acid.

words.definition: a fatty acid containing two or more carbon-carbon double bonds
words.example: Polyunsaturated fatty acids contain several bends in their hydrocarbon chains.

words.definition: connective tissue specialized for storing triglycerides in fat cells
words.example: Adipose tissue stores energy and provides thermal insulation.

words.definition: having both hydrophilic and hydrophobic regions
words.example: Phospholipids are amphipathic molecules.

words.definition: a lipid with a characteristic structure of four fused carbon rings
words.example: Cholesterol is a steroid that influences membrane properties.

words.definition: an organic molecule with an amino group, a carboxyl group and a variable side chain attached to a central carbon
words.example: Proteins are assembled from amino-acid monomers.

words.definition: the central carbon atom of an amino acid bonded to the amino group, carboxyl group, hydrogen and R group
words.example: The R group attached to the alpha carbon differs among amino acids.

words.definition: a nitrogen-containing functional group that is part of the general structure of an amino acid
words.example: The amine group can accept a proton under biological conditions.

words.definition: an acidic functional group containing a carbon atom double-bonded to oxygen and bonded to a hydroxyl group
words.example: Every standard amino acid contains a carboxyl group.

words.definition: the variable side chain of an amino acid that determines many of its chemical properties
words.example: Different R groups make amino acids hydrophobic, polar or charged.

words.definition: a covalent bond formed between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of another
words.example: Peptide bonds link amino acids in a polypeptide.

words.definition: a molecule formed when two amino acids are joined by one peptide bond
words.example: A condensation reaction between two amino acids forms a dipeptide.

words.definition: a chain of amino acids linked by peptide bonds
words.example: A polypeptide folds to produce a functional protein or protein subunit.

words.definition: an amino acid that an organism cannot synthesize in sufficient amounts and must obtain from its diet
words.example: Humans must obtain essential amino acids from food.

words.definition: an amino acid that an organism can synthesize in sufficient amounts
words.example: The human body can make many non-essential amino acids.

words.definition: a sequence of amino acids connected by peptide bonds
words.example: The amino-acid sequence of a peptide chain affects its final function.

words.definition: loss of a protein's normal three-dimensional shape and function caused by disruption of stabilizing interactions
words.example: High temperature can denature an enzyme and reduce its activity.
